thread:
Alex: PSA: the new office coffee machine has a config file. Its YAML. Of course it is. :coffee:
Casey: Oh no. Were going to end up with `unexpected indent` on our cappuccinos. :grimacing:
Morgan: Found this taped to the machine:```yaml
brew:
  strength: bold
  cups: 4
   schedule: 
     - 08:30
     - 13:00
```
Taylor: That extra space before `schedule` is going to cause a 5am incident. :sweat_smile:
Alex: Also the button labels are `deploy`, `revert`, `force`. Press the wrong one and it tries to redeploy the grinder.
Casey: I legitimately tried `brew --force` once and it spit out espresso and a compiler warning. :joy:
Morgan: DevOpsBot, are we supposed to run `brew build` in the kitchen? :robot_face:
DevOpsBot: @Morgan please do not run build commands on shared appliances. Side effects include: burned toast, stale jokes, and mysterious merge conflicts. :warning:
Taylor: Can someone add `.coffeeignore` to the repo? Im tired of beans showing up in PRs.
Alex: Also vote: rename the darkest roast `segfault-dark` or `null-pointer-napalm`? :one: for segfault, :two: for null-pointer
Casey: `segfault-dark` wins by taste.
Morgan: If the machine returns `core dumped`, is that an SLO violation? :thinking_face:
DevOpsBot: incident created: #coffee-core-dump — priority: low, severity: emotional.
Taylor: Whoever wrote the YAML also used tabs in one place. I will never trust that brew again.
Alex: New rule: if your YAML makes the coffee, you get the first cup. No exceptions. :coffee::star2:
Casey: Adding that to the handbook now. "Troubleshooting: check indentation, then your life choices"
Morgan: TL;DR: coffee is now a compiled artifact. Ship it with tests. :white_check_mark:
